title: Playlist Manager
story: DJ Mode activated! You need to build a playlist manager — add songs, remove the one everyone's tired of, hit shuffle for a random track, and queue up the next banger. The crowd is waiting!
why: Playlists combine Vec operations (add, remove, access by index) with practical algorithms like linear search for removal and random index selection — foundational patterns for any ordered collection.
analogy: A playlist is like a stack of vinyl records — you put new ones on top, take one out if you don't like it, close your eyes and grab a random one (shuffle), or just flip to the next in order.
try_it: Add an `artist` field to each song by using a Map[Str, Str] that maps song titles to artist names. Update `remove_song` to also clean up the artist Map. Then write a `find_by_artist` function that returns all songs by a given artist. For bonus: implement `move_to_top` that moves a song to the front of the playlist.
tips: Removing from a Vec by value requires a rebuild — filter into a new Vec, then copy back
Use deterministic math for "random" in playgrounds: `(len * prime + offset) % len` gives a consistent index
`.get(index)` returns `Option[T]` — safer than direct indexing since it handles out-of-bounds gracefully
common_mistakes: Trying to remove during a for loop over the same Vec — this corrupts iteration; always build a new Vec
Calling `.get(index)` without checking `len` first — if empty, `get(0)` returns None
Forgetting to clear the original Vec after filtering — you'll end up with duplicate entries
